newsitem.title: SWEDEN: POLL - MODO H1 PROFIT SEEN DOWN 48 PCT.
newsitem.headline: POLL - MODO H1 PROFIT SEEN DOWN 48 PCT.

text.p: Swedish forestry company MoDo was expected to post a 48 percent lower profit after financial items of 884 million crowns for the first half of 1997, a Reuters poll of 14 analysts found on Friday.
Forecasts varied between 820 million crowns and one billion crowns. The 884 million crown forecast compares to a 1.66 billion crown profit for the first half of 1996.
For the full year analysts estimated a profit after financial items of 1.92 billion crowns, which is a 34 percent drop from 2.92 billion crowns in full year 1996.

Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Aragon, Aros, Carnegie, CI Nordic, Den Norske Bank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, James Capel, Kleinwort Benson, Matteus, Nordiska, Paribas, and Salomon Brothers.
Modo's half year report is due to be released on Thursday, August 14.
